title: Two-member committee: two independently trained localizers must agree before a fix is trusted; confidence is the smaller of the two members' belief on the consensus block
hypothesis: The stage no experiment in this era has questioned is the confidence gate, and it is where the score is being lost. On the held-out 2024 photograph the false-fix rate has sat at 39-43% through three different training designs (exp 4: 38.75%, exp 5: 42.25%, exp 6: 43.0%) while usable sat at 12-14%; false fixes cost three times what usable fixes earn, and converting a false fix into an abstention is worth exactly as much to the mission score as finding a new usable fix. The single model's confidence is the pooled softmax mass of one classifier trained only on photographs it has memorised, so on a photograph it has not seen it is uninformative by construction: the founding measurement showed the 0.040 champion 97% confident while wrong, with 390 confident predictions on a foreign photograph collapsing onto 40 cells. That is the signature of a model that, given a foreign input, slides into whichever survey-specific shortcut the input happens to trigger. A different model, trained from a different random start on differently drawn augmentations, has different shortcuts and slides into different cells for the same foreign frame, while on frames where the shared street-and-building geometry genuinely names the cell both models land on the same block. Disagreement between independently trained models is the one uncertainty estimator the literature finds robust under dataset shift (deep ensembles, Lakshminarayanan et al. 2017; Ovadia et al. 2019 measured it dominating every learned or post-hoc calibrated single-model confidence as shift grows): it is epistemic uncertainty, which is what a never-seen survey produces, not aleatoric. The library (L2) lists learned aleatoric confidence as what does NOT transfer under map change, and the earlier eras' two honesty attempts were exactly that kind: four-area exp 15 (a field-shape confidence head) and exp 32 (abstention thresholds calibrated on never-trained blocks) re-score at 1.85 and 1.77 on this ruler, 85% and 77% false fix. No era has tried an ensemble (nothing in lineage_history mentions one). This is also materially different from the decode-time consensus the Prignitz detour refuted: that averaged ONE model's belief over four rotations of the same frame, and a wrong answer that is rotation-stable survives it; here two separately trained models are asked the same question, and a wrong answer must be shared by both to survive. Cost, measured at design time without training (runs/_probe_exp7_committee.py): two members with trunk widths [3,24,48,96,112] export to 3,942,411 bytes (3.76 MiB, under the 4 MiB gate) at 1.97 ms host latency, 971,864 parameters, versus the single 160-wide model's 3,080,677 bytes and 1.49 ms. Each member is narrower than today's single model (head 112x2970 = 333k vs 475k), so per-member fit on the training photographs will be somewhat lower; the committee's averaged belief is expected to recover most of it. The design is honest about what it targets: it attacks the false-fix term, not the usable term, and it is the gate every later accuracy experiment will also need.
method: ONE change: model/model.py's CellLocNet becomes a committee of N_MEMBERS = 2 fully independent members (each = the current 4-stage stride-2 conv trunk at chans [3,24,48,96,112] + its own 2970-way cell head + its own offset head; no shared weights). Deployed decode in forward(): per-member softmax p_k; averaged belief pbar = mean_k p_k; argmax cell of pbar; the existing 3x3 block mask around it; conf = min over members of (p_k * mask).sum() - each member must independently put its belief on the consensus block; the fix is pbar's mass-weighted centroid of the block plus the mean of the members' offsets. Training (model/train.py): each mini-batch is cut once, then each member receives its OWN independent augment_views() draw of those crops and its own loss (soft tent cross-entropy + residual offset target computed from that member's own logits, exactly as today); the total loss is the sum over members, one optimiser step. Members differ by random initialisation (sequential construction from the seeded RNG) and by their augmentation draws; there is no agreement term in the loss, because diversity is the mechanism. Per-member top1 and the member-agreement rate (same argmax cell) are logged per epoch. Views per epoch, paired three-survey chunks, augmentation ranges, targets, schedule, epochs, CLI and the ONNX contract are untouched.
expected_outcome: Primary (held-out truedop_2024): 1.271 -> predicted 1.05-1.18, through the false-fix rate: 38.75% -> 18-28% as frames on which the two members name different blocks become abstentions, with usable_fix_rate roughly flat (11.75% -> 9-14%; the averaged belief is at least as accurate as one member, and genuinely-right frames are where members agree). 2024 coverage falls from 0.505 to a predicted 0.28-0.40; the 0.2 FAIL floor is the explicit risk of this design and is flagged, not hidden - if the committee abstains on nearly all of today's confident-wrong frames AND on some of the confident-right ones, coverage approaches the floor. Median 2024 error among confident frames (1,911 m) should fall below 800 m because the surviving confident set is enriched for correct fixes. Training diagnostics (bb_dop20 / truedop_2022 / truedop_2023 = 0.733 / 0.673 / 0.518 on exp 4): coverage drops further (narrower members, and the min gate), usable 36-54% -> 30-50%, false fix 6-9% -> 2-5%; a lower false-fix rate on the training photographs at held-out viewpoints is itself evidence the gate works. Mechanical checks that must hold or the mechanism did not bite: the two logged per-member top1 values end within ~0.05 of each other and of exp 4's 0.45; the logged member agreement rate on training views ends at or above 0.6; exported bytes read ~3,942,411 (well under 4,194,304) and host latency ~2 ms. Decision rules: (a) 2024 false fix falls by >= 8 points with usable within +-3 points -> supported; the committee is the confidence gate from here on, and the next experiment attacks ACCURACY on top of it with external features (cached DINOv2 patch distillation, library L2 #3, or a permissively-licensed pretrained trunk), which no experiment of this era has tried. (b) 2024 coverage < 0.2 (score FAIL) -> the min gate over-abstains; retry once with the geometric mean of the two block masses in place of the min, nothing else changed. (c) 2024 false fix stays >= 35% -> the members share their confusions: confident-wrong frames are look-alike places both members confuse the same way, not survey-shortcut attractors, and no amount of ensembling reaches them; the next move is external features. Standing check: the score must move through false_fix_rate with usable_fix_rate not falling by more than the false-fix gain; if the score improves while neither product rate moves, the metric is wrong again.
eli5: Instead of one navigator the drone now carries two, trained separately on the same three photographs of Berlin: each starts from a different random state and sees every training picture under its own random lighting and blur, so each picks up its own habits and blind spots. When a brand-new photograph fools a navigator, it tends to fool each one differently, so they point at different places; the drone then says 'not sure' and waits for the next frame instead of flying on a wrong fix. Only when both navigators point at the same place does the drone accept it. It is the same reason you ask two witnesses separately: two independent accounts that agree are worth far more than one confident voice.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: NEW: two independent small strided conv stacks, each slightly narrower than before (112 channels at the top instead of 160), sharing no weights; each turns the frame into its own compact fingerprint

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: NEW: each extractor feeds its own scorer over all ~3,000 128 m map tiles of Berlin; the two tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: NEW: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: each member is trained on its own independently re-photographed version (brightness, contrast, blur, grain) of every training view, with its own tile-and-offset loss; the two losses are summed and no term asks the members to agree, so they keep different habits. Paired three-survey batches, targets, schedule and views per epoch unchanged.

implementation_brief:
FILES: model/model.py and model/train.py only. Read runs/_probe_exp7_committee.py first: it contains a working, export-verified reference of the Member and Committee forward passes (3,942,411 B at chans [3,24,48,96,112]); lift from it rather than re-deriving.

=== model/model.py ===
1. Add module constants N_MEMBERS = 2 and MEMBER_CHANS = [3, 24, 48, 96, 112]. Keep CELL_PX, grid_dims(), build_model(), loss_fn() (signature AND body unchanged), export_onnx() and estimate_position() exactly as they are. Update the module docstring to describe the committee decode (keep the contract paragraph: 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1] -> [[u, v, conf]], u/v normalised map coords, conf in [0,1]; whole decode inside the graph).
2. New class Member(nn.Module): __init__(self, n_cells, chans=MEMBER_CHANS) builds self.features = the current trunk verbatim (for cin,cout in zip(chans, chans[1:]): Conv2d(cin,cout,3,stride=2,padding=1) + BatchNorm2d + ReLU(inplace)), self.cls_head = nn.Linear(chans[-1], n_cells), self.off_head = nn.Linear(chans[-1], 2). forward(self, x): f = self.features(x).mean(dim=(2,3)); return self.cls_head(f), torch.tanh(self.off_head(f)) * 0.5 (the current training_outputs body).
3. CellLocNet.__init__: keep gw, gh, n_cells, the cell_u/cell_v buffers and scale_u/scale_v exactly as now; replace self.features/self.cls_head/self.off_head with self.members = nn.ModuleList(Member(self.n_cells) for _ in range(N_MEMBERS)). Do NOT re-seed between members; sequential construction from the already-seeded torch RNG gives each a different init.
4. Add CellLocNet.block_mask(self, idx): given argmax cell indices idx [B] (int64), return the float [B, n_cells] 3x3 block mask using the existing 1.6-pitch Chebyshev rule (the du/dv/mask lines currently in forward()). forward() and train.py's residual_offset_target both use it so the geometry stays single-sourced.
5. CellLocNet.training_outputs(self, x) -> list of N_MEMBERS (logits, offset) tuples, one per member, all on the same x.
6. CellLocNet.forward(self, x) (the DEPLOYED path, returns [B,3]): outs = self.training_outputs(x); ps = [F.softmax(l, dim=1) for l,_ in outs]; pbar = torch.stack(ps, 0).mean(0); idx = pbar.argmax(dim=1); mask = self.block_mask(idx); masses = torch.stack([(p * mask).sum(dim=1) for p in ps], 0)  # [N_MEMBERS, B]; conf = masses.min(dim=0).values  # each member's own mass on the consensus block, take the smaller; q = pbar * mask; w = q / q.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-9); off = torch.stack([o for _,o in outs], 0).mean(0); u = (w * cell_u).sum(1) + off[:,0]*scale_u; v likewise; return torch.stack([u.clamp(0,1), v.clamp(0,1), conf], dim=1). conf is a min of sub-sums of softmaxes so it stays in [0,1]. This exact graph exported cleanly with opset 17, dynamo=False in the probe.

=== model/train.py ===
7. residual_offset_target(model, logits, pos, meta): keep its logic but replace the inline du/dv/mask lines with mask = model.block_mask(idx); it is called ONCE PER MEMBER with that member's own logits (each member's offset target mirrors its own argmax, as the single model's did).
8. run_epoch(): per mini-batch, cut the crops ONCE: xb0 = gpu_crops(scene, cap_b, cx[idx], cy[idx], ang[idx]). soft_t = make_soft_targets(pb, ...) once. Then for k, member in enumerate(model.members): xb_k = augment_views(xb0)  (a fresh independent random draw per member; do not reuse one augmented batch for both); logits_k, off_k = member(xb_k); off_t_k = residual_offset_target(model, logits_k, pb, meta); loss_k = loss_fn(logits_k, off_k, soft_t, off_t_k). loss = sum of loss_k; single opt.zero_grad(); loss.backward(); opt.step(). Keep every tensor on the device inside the loop - no .item()/.cpu()/int()/float() on device tensors in the step loop (the 2026-10-31 device discipline in the docstring).
9. Stats (all accumulated as device tensors, read once at epoch end like today): loss_sum (sum loss * B); the committee's top1 vs the containing cell from pbar = mean of the member softmaxes (this feeds 'correct', cap_correct/cap_seen and the existing top1_by_capture log exactly as now); conf_sum from pbar's max (mean_max_softmax, as now); NEW member_correct [N_MEMBERS] (each member's own argmax == cb) and NEW agree (count of views where member 0's and member 1's argmax cells coincide). Return them in the stats dict; print per epoch: loss, top1, mean_max_softmax, views, lr, top1_by_capture, member_top1=[...], agree_rate=... .
10. train_area(): unchanged except the returned info dict gains 'n_members': N_MEMBERS, 'member_chans': MEMBER_CHANS, 'final_member_top1': [...], 'final_member_agree_rate': float, and 'capture_sampling' gains the phrase ', two-member committee with independent augmentation draws per member'. Keep the keys 'final_train_top1', 'final_train_top1_by_capture', 'augmentation', 'captures', 'init': 'from-scratch' etc. exactly as they are. Import N_MEMBERS, MEMBER_CHANS from model.model.
11. Update train.py's module docstring with a short COMMITTEE paragraph (what, why: epistemic disagreement as the confidence gate under a change of photograph).

=== UNTOUCHED ===
chunk_views, gpu_crops, augment_views and AUG, make_soft_targets, CHUNK_SIZE, BATCH_SIZE, Adam lr 1e-3 + cosine schedule, epochs, load_scene (training reads ONLY buckets(meta, 'train'); nothing under model/ may open the eval capture in any form), the CLI (--area --out-dir --data-dir --epochs --max-crops-per-bucket --seed), export path <out>/models/<area>.onnx, train_info.json append semantics, loss_fn.

=== CHECKS BEFORE EXIT ===
(i) .venv/bin/python -c "import model.train, model.model"; (ii) size gate: build the model with load_meta('berlin', DATA_DIR) and export_onnx() to a temp path, print the byte size: expected ~3,942,411; it MUST be < 4,194,304 - if it is above 4,100,000 for any reason, set MEMBER_CHANS = [3, 24, 48, 96, 104] (3,696,843 B measured) and re-check; (iii) run the exported graph once through onnxruntime on a zeros frame and confirm the output is [1,3] with conf in [0,1]; (iv) a 1-chunk smoke of run_epoch is fine (max_chunks=1) but do NOT run full training - the harness does that.
